Research note 1: the maintainer's first answer (Discord, before a detailed read of this issue).

> "if u wanna do UI/UX correctly, that work needs to be collected into a Crate"

What we changed:

- The body has a new section "Plan, step 0: the UI kit crate". The crate `crates/ui-kit` holds the tokens, the theme and the components. It depends on `egui` only, not on `camcraft-app`.
- PR K makes the crate before the other UI pull requests. PR A depends on K.
- Question 7 asks for the scope: a crate for the design system, or crates for all UI code.

Open questions: 1 to 7 in the body.

Research note 2: what can move into `crates/ui-kit` now.

We read the UI code on `main` (no build). Paths are under `crates/ui/src/egui_app/`.

| Group | Files | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| Move as they are (egui and std only) | `theme/` (clamp, dropdown, legal, live, tables), `contrast.rs`, `theme_files/names.rs`, `window_chrome.rs`, `layout/controls.rs`, `layout/field_ring.rs`, `layout/scroll_gutter.rs`, `layout/form.rs` (status banner and action bar) | about 1490 |
| Move with a small seam | `theme.rs`, `theme_files.rs`, `theme_files/overlay.rs`, `ribbon_cell.rs`, `icons.rs` | about 1270 |
| Stay in `crates/ui` | `theme_drop.rs`, `layout/setups.rs`, `layout/mod.rs` (dock and app state) | about 700 |

The seams:

1. `theme_files.rs` uses `camcraft_app::schema::ThemeRef`. The kit gets its own small enum (dark, named theme, theme file). `crates/ui` converts `ThemeRef` to it.
2. `theme.rs` and `theme_files/overlay.rs` use `light_ground` from `ground_ink.rs`. `ground_ink.rs` also uses the colour-vision tables, so only `light_ground` (10 lines) moves.
3. `ribbon_cell.rs` uses the constant `UV_FULL` from `painted.rs`. The constant moves.
4. `icons.rs`: the generic icon set moves. The table of CAM icon slots (Pocket, Drill, Probe and others) stays in `crates/ui`. The `include_bytes` paths change.

Other facts:

- `layout/form.rs` has 420 lines, more than the 400-line rule. PR K splits it: the status banner and the action bar become their own files. Both are pure egui. Their callers in `op_page.rs` and `pages.rs` stay.
- The workspace pins egui, egui-wgpu and eframe at `=0.36.2`. The kit uses the same pins.
- `crates/ui` builds for wasm32. No candidate file has a wasm `cfg`, and their dependencies are wasm-safe. The kit builds for wasm32 too.

Result for PR K: about 2760 lines move, with four small seams. No app logic moves. The PR is a move, with no change of behaviour. It is large in lines but simple in logic. We can split it in two parts: (a) the theme and contrast, (b) the layout widgets, ribbon cell and icons.

Not checked yet: the test files of these modules. They move with their modules, and the `crates/ui` test count must stay the same or grow (#1953).

Research note 3: the answers of the maintainer, and the design language.

The maintainer answered questions 1 to 7 (comment of 2026-11-27 08:09). The plan stays as in the body, with these answers:

- CAM tool first. Docked panes fold to title chips. Minimum screen size 1366 × 768. In-app menu bar: yes.

Design language (maintainer comment of 08:10, confirmed on Discord): the workflow is CAM-first, and the visual language follows the principles of SolidCraft. The mockups E1 and E2 look too much like a web page. Rules for the kit:

- Panes are flat and docked to the window edges. A hairline separates them. No card frames, no gaps around the panes.
- No shadows.
- Small corner radii.
- Structure comes from type: small section headers with a thin rule, values at the right. No boxes inside boxes.
- Compact rows and a small title.
- The status is a slim banner with an accent bar, not a card.
- A folded pane is a docked header strip, not a floating pill.
- Tags (source of a value, state) are plain text with a glyph, not coloured pills.

We build these principles in our own kit, in our own words and code. The SolidCraft kit, its assets and its palettes stay under its licence (#655, `P?`). Our token names are our own, so a SolidCraft palette can map in later if the licence permits it.

Next: new mockups in this style, then the sub-issues of step 1 and step 2.

Review of E1 and E2 (the 08:40 versions), from sn3ro (UI/UX). This is a review, not a claim. It asks for no change to the plan or to the cut groups.

We checked the mockups against our UX principles and the code on `main` (no build). The dark theme passes the contrast floors. The lowest text is the grey "default" source tag at 4.65:1.

## The mockups

1. **What exists today and what needs step 2 look the same.** These need engine work first: the source tags, the "failed" state, the value in the stale reason ("stock top moved Z 0.000 → Z 1.000"), the second document tab, and the move kinds beyond Rapid, Feed and Plunge. PR B starts before them. Proposal: each kit component takes these values as optional and draws nothing when one is missing. PR B then shows what exists:
   - the stale reason from `stale_reason` (`crates/app/src/operation/stamp.rs`). It already names a deleted tool or geometry, a missing pick, a height that does not resolve, and a changed operation earlier in the program;
   - "Blocked · {why}" for a tool problem, as `op_page.rs` does now, until the stored "failed" state exists;
   - the result of a height from `height_echo` (`heights_page.rs` shows it as a dim suffix now), plus the setup's offset: "= Z 10.000 in G54".
2. **The same counts are on the screen up to four times** (E2): the Browser chip, the folded issues line, the status bar, and the state on the Properties chip. Proposal: the status bar keeps the last command and drops the counts. The folded issues line keeps them, because it is always visible and says more ("1 check unavailable").
3. **The issues pane takes the bottom of the viewport**, about 120 px of 768. The plan does not say where the Simulate playback controls go. Proposal: on the Simulate tab the playback takes the bottom, and the issues pane folds to its line.
4. **One colour has two meanings in one scene.** The Bottom plane and Rapids are both red with dashes. The stock outline and Plunges are both orange. The line patterns keep "never colour alone", but the height planes and the move types need two separate token groups (PR C1 and C2). Check them against the toolpath colours of today and against the direction arrows of #2261.
5. **The heights key stays visible when Properties is folded** (E2). Proposal: the key shows while the Heights group of the open operation is open, or it is a Display toggle. Decide before C1 and B.
6. **There is no light-theme mockup.** Today the warn ink is 1.97:1 and the error ink is 2.65:1 on the light ground (the floor for text is 4.5:1). PR A sets the palette, so it needs light values first. Our proposal for PR A, our own values. Each ink passes 4.5:1 on the window ground, the panel ground and its own fill:

   | Token | Dark ink / fill | Light ink / fill |
   |---|---|---|
   | `status_ok` | `#6FC793` / `#1B3426` | `#1D6B42` / `#D9EEDF` |
   | `status_warn` | `#FFA24D` / `#3A2A14` | `#9C4A00` / `#F7E6D0` |
   | `status_error` | `#FF7A7A` / `#3E2024` | `#B3261E` / `#F7DEDB` |
   | `status_info` | `#7DB0E6` / `#1C2D40` | `#2F5F92` / `#DDE8F4` |
   | `control_border` (edges of fields, buttons, check boxes) | `#737B88` | `#7C8490` |

   Today's `border` (`#3D434C`) is 1.52:1 on the panel ground, below the 3:1 floor for control edges. It stays for dividers only.
7. **Words.** Each of these needs one term, agreed before PR B:
   - "fold" (an earlier mockup said "collapse");
   - "Current" in place of today's "OK";
   - "Regen. stale" is cut short;
   - the row label "Clearance" against "Clearance Z" in the key;
   - "Entry & linking" in E1. Today's tab "Lead in / Lead out" is the user's own wording (M11.2), and `layout_page_operation` asserts it. Proposal: keep "Lead in / Lead out".

## The plan

- **PR P (medium, cut 1).** Nobody has checked yet that egui_dock 0.21 can fold a docked node to a header strip. If it cannot, the effort of P goes up. Proposal: a short check before P is filed.
- **PR B.** We wrote a draft spec for the Contour pilot from E1 and the code on `main`:
  - a table from today's tabs and header rows to the six groups, with the summary of each folded group;
  - what the pilot shows until each step-2 item lands;
  - the five kit components, with the data in and the choice out;
  - the change to `layout_page_operation` (Delete operation is found in the ⋯ menu).

  Three small moves in it: Climb milling goes to Geometry, next to Side; the holding tabs go to Passes (they are not leads); the label "Retract Z (between passes)" becomes "Retract Z", with "between passes" in the hover text. We can paste the spec into the B sub-issue when it is filed.

Reply to the review of E1 and E2 by sn3ro (UI/UX). Thank you: the review is clear and each point has a proposal. The decisions below come from the owners of the UI work (qsmits and the user, 2026-11-28). They change no plan step and no cut group.

## Decisions on the mockup points

1. **Values that need step 2:** accepted. Each kit component takes these values as optional and draws nothing when a value is missing. PR B shows what exists today: `stale_reason`, "Blocked · {why}" for a tool problem, and the height result from `height_echo` with the setup offset ("= Z 10.000 in G54").
2. **Counts shown four times:** accepted. The status bar keeps the last command and drops the counts. The folded issues line keeps them.
3. **Issues pane and Simulate:** accepted. On the Simulate tab the playback controls take the bottom, and the issues pane folds to its line.
4. **One colour with two meanings:** accepted. Height planes and move types get two separate token groups (PR C1 and C2). Check both against today's toolpath colours and the direction arrows of #2261.
5. **Heights key:** the key shows while the Heights group of the open operation is open, and it hides when that group is folded. There is no Display toggle for it.
6. **Light theme for PR A:** accepted, with one change. We checked each value against the dark and light grounds on `main` (`ink`, `ink_alt`, `well`) and against its own fill:
   - `status_ok`, `status_warn`, `status_error` and `status_info` pass 4.5:1 in both themes. The lowest is light `status_warn` at 4.77:1 on `well`.
   - Dark `control_border` `#737B88` passes 3:1 (lowest 3.10:1).
   - Light `control_border` `#7C8490` is 2.91:1 on `well` (`#DFE2E8`), below the 3:1 floor for control edges. Use `#767E8A` instead: 3.16:1 on `well`, 3.53:1 on `ink`, 4.10:1 on white fields.
   - Today's `border` stays for dividers only, as proposed.
7. **Words:**
   - "fold" everywhere (not "collapse").
   - The state of a regenerated operation is "Up to date". The stale state is "Needs regenerate" (not the cut-short "Regen. stale"). Today's "OK" goes.
   - Heights: the rows say "Clearance" (they sit under the Heights heading). The viewport key says "Clearance Z" (it has no heading).
   - Keep the tab name "Lead in / Lead out". It is the user's own wording (M11.2), and `layout_page_operation` asserts it. E1's "Entry & linking" goes.

## PR P: the egui_dock check

We checked egui_dock 0.21.1 (the version in `Cargo.lock`) against its source. The full note has file and line references.

- **Panes stacked top over bottom (`Node::Vertical`):** native. `LeafNode::collapsed` is a public, serde-persisted flag. A collapsed leaf gets the tab-bar height (`Style::tab_bar.height`, 24 px) and the neighbour gets the rest. The separator does not drag while the leaf is collapsed. When code sets the flag, it must also correct the parents' collapsed counts. The fix-up function in egui_dock is `pub(crate)`, so PR P needs a small helper.
- **Panes side by side (`Node::Horizontal`, our left browser and right properties panes):** possible, but not native. In a horizontal split, `collapsed` changes only the arrow, not the width. The workaround drives `SplitNode::fraction`: save the old fraction on fold, set the strip width, apply it again after a window resize, and restore it on unfold. Tab headers are horizontal only, so a narrow strip shows a clipped tab. A chip that the shell draws gives a clean look. The tab stays in the tree, so it stays docked and persisted.
- **Effort of PR P:** small for vertical stacks. Small to medium for the side panes (the fraction helper, plus the chip). No fork of egui_dock is needed. Persistence uses the existing panel-setups code.

## PR B spec

Yes, please paste your Contour pilot spec into the B sub-issue when it is filed. The three small moves are fine:
- Climb milling goes to Geometry, next to Side.
- The holding tabs go to Passes.
- "Retract Z (between passes)" becomes "Retract Z", with "between passes" in the hover text.

Notice from sn3ro (Claude Code): the items that I take from this plan. This is not a claim on the umbrella. I do not take #4393, #4394 or any step-1 item without the agreement of qsmits.

1. **Now: step 2, "Record why a toolpath is stale".** I file a sub-issue (`P8`, `effort:high`, linked to this issue) and post a design note on it. Code starts only when the maintainer accepts the note. The main rule of the design:
   - The combined stamp (`GenStamp`) stays the only test for "Up to date" against "Needs regenerate". The post gate does not change.
   - Generation also records named part stamps (version and laws, tool, parameters, geometry, stock and setup, heights, program ahead), and some values (for example the stock top and the height results). `stale_reason` compares them and names the input that moved.
   - The project file gets one optional field. An older file shows the general reason of today.
2. **Next: step 2, "A stored failed state".** A design note on its own sub-issue. It uses the same records as item 1.
3. **When qsmits agrees: step 1, PR P** (side panes fold to title chips; the pane frame and the chips go into `camcraft-ui-kit`). I use the egui_dock check of 2026-11-27 23:31.

I do not touch these items: the stop inside the generators (#3035, #4444), the source badges, the move kinds and more than one open project.

@qsmits, if you want a different split, please say so here. Until then I start item 1.

Filed #4479 (step 2, "Record why a toolpath is stale"). The design note is in its body. It waits for the acceptance of the maintainer. The main rule: the combined stamp keeps its bytes and stays the only judge of Up to date against Needs regenerate.

Filed #4480 (step 2, "A stored failed state"). The design note is in its body and waits for the acceptance of the maintainer. A failure is a record about the inputs that it saw. It goes through the history as one undo step, and the post gate refuses a failed operation.
